_about: H-taste -> the sore spots (1 Oct play-test D15e, decision 27; js/clinic/heal/games/taste.js). Pop the spots of the colour(s) said with a cotton bud dipped in a soothing ointment (never a pin), the others stay; then one named drink (a liquid poured, one thing added, stirred, given) clears the rest. Levels are data: pop (colours to pop; L3 every colour but the one said, na), each (spots of each popping colour), decoys (spots of each other colour), upMs (how long a spot stays up), maxUp (spots up at once), counts (spoons of the drink's thing, from L2). The colours are data/clinic.json's col-* words (English placeholders, to record). art: the art plan's M2 tongue, O2 spots and O3 bud swap in by file name once ready.

budClean._about: s08-w5b (CLN-195; Zafar 18 Oct: 'a clean cotton bud with nothing on it ... when it hits the blob ... the colour of the blob'): the s08b clean bud, lying across its picture; tip = the right swab's middle, swab = its half length and half height (shares of the picture, measured on its alpha); the code tints that swab with the colour of the spot it last touched

glass._about: s08 wave 7B (CLN-196, Zafar 19 Oct: yes, the metal cup; the new cup with no drop shadow, sitting on the surface): the s08c steel cup TC1 (build/tools/art/specs/s08c.cut.json tc1-steel-cup), opaque, so the drink is drawn in its mouth only (opaque; lip = the rim's thickness, a share of w). rim = the rim's ellipse (centre x, y, half axes as shares of the picture's w and h, measured on the cut's alpha: top row 3, widest at rows 83-100, the near edge at row 192); inside = the drink's surface when full and the floor's centre (y), the inner half widths there (of w; the floor's visible back edge at row 159, 107-292 wide) and the surface's height over its width (the rim's ry over rx)

camera._about: D2 (1 Oct): the wide shot the zoom starts from, chosen by the angle the close-up needs (front-on or side-on). No side-on sitting pose exists yet: 'side' uses the front pose until the art batch (art list A1).
camera._target: A1 (5 Oct): the match cut. target = where the close-up draws the sore part and size = its radius, in the close-up's 800 x 500 units: the push-in ends with the patient's part (from the art's anchor) at that place and size.
